title: Contact Book Entry
story: Your phone contacts are a mess — duplicate names, missing emails, wrong numbers. You decide to build a clean contact system where each entry has a name, phone, and email. You want to search by name and display contacts in a uniform format.
why: A struct with a search method teaches the pattern of data + filtering, used in every app.
analogy: A Contact is like a business card. The display method reads the card aloud. The matches method checks if "Alice" is written on the front — if so, you've found the right card in your Rolodex.
try_it: Add a `Contact.initials(self) -> Str` method that returns the first letter of each word in the name (e.g., "Alice Chen" ? "AC"). Add your top 3 real contacts. Add a `Contact.has_email(self) -> Bool` method that checks if email is not empty.
tips: Use `==` to compare strings for exact matches — it checks character-by-character
The `|` character is a common delimiter for contact display — use spaces around it for readability
Name your method `matches` not `search` — it asks the contact "do you match this?"
common_mistakes: Using `=` instead of `==` for comparison — single `=` is assignment, `==` checks equality
Forgetting to return `Bool` from `matches` — the return type must be `-> Bool`
